title: Markov chain graph
$comment: The chain walks over DISCRETE states (crop x stage). CONTINUOUS variables (soil, climate, finances) live in the node and change only through effects: what the chain can alter is whatever appears as an effect target. The chain holds no seed and makes no choice by itself: a scenario policy (monte_carlo.json) decides which edge to take, deterministically (rotation) or by drawing from 'probability' (markov).

id.description: Chain id. Generated chains use the profile id.

profile.description: Profile the chain was generated for (profile.json id). Absent in hand-written examples.

provenance.description: How the chain was produced: source files, rule and its parameters.

node.description: The state of one Monte Carlo trajectory at a point in time: what the field looks like now. Behaviour: (1) Monte Carlo creates one node per trajectory from a profile (soil, climate at day 0, finances at 0). (2) Entering a state applies its 'entry' effects. (3) While in the state, 'rate' effects accumulate over duration_days and Monte Carlo refreshes climate each period. (4) Leaving applies 'exit' effects. (5) Outgoing edges are filtered by 'when' against the node, one is drawn, its effects apply, and the loop repeats until the horizon. Why it exists: crops, actions and climate must affect each other (soybean adds N used by maize, liming unlocks soybean, drought cuts yield). They can only do that through one shared place. A field belongs here only if some effect writes it or some condition reads it.

state.description: id of the current discrete state

yield.description: Expected yield of the current crop. Starts from PAM yield; effects such as water stress or pests multiply it. Revenue at exit = yield x price.

price.description: Sale price for the current crop. Source: PAM real price (IPCA-adjusted); Yahoo futures as reference.

state.description: Discrete state: one crop in one stage. With stage 'skip_stages' the state is the sum of all stages: only entry and exit (see effect 'at'), duration = full cycle, no intermediate granularity.

id.description: Convention: '<crop>:<stage>'. Generated from the crop list of a profile (v1 crop-transition-markov.json states) x the stages with data; today every crop has only skip_stages.

crop.description: Crop id, same ids as v1 (soybean, maize_grain, sugarcane, coffee, brachiaria, ...)

duration_days.description: Time spent in this state. Effects with operation=rate are multiplied by it.

effects.description: Applied while the trajectory stays in this state

transition.description: Graph edge. Probabilities leaving one state (for the same 'action') must sum to 1 after filtering by 'when'; consumers renormalize.

action.description: id of the action that enables this edge; null = natural transition

probability.description: Markov chain parameter: chance of taking this edge once the trajectory leaves 'from'. Estimated from data (e.g. PAM counts / outgoing_count) or set as a prior. Monte Carlo does not set it: it only draws with its seed which edge each trajectory takes.

count.description: Whole observed transitions behind the edge, when there are any (v1: year pairs in which the municipality's dominant crop went from 'from' to 'to').

mass.description: Fractional evidence behind the edge when it is not a whole count (v1: sum over consecutive years of area share of 'from' x area share of 'to' among the top-5 PAM crops, which assumes independence).

outgoing_mass.description: Total mass leaving 'from' over the destinations kept in the chain. probability = mass / outgoing_mass.

when.description: Edge exists only if the node meets every condition (e.g. pH < 5.5 blocks planting)

effects.description: Applied once, when the edge is crossed (e.g. harvest revenue)

provenance.description: Where the probability comes from, specific enough to check it (dataset, year pairs, rule or prior reference).
